newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Autoliv sees continued strong growth.
newsitem.headline: Autoliv sees continued strong growth.

text.p: Swedish car safety equipment company Autoliv, which is merging with the car safety operations of U.S. Morton, said on Monday it sees continued strong growth, both in the U.S. and Europe.

"The new company will keep growing both in the U.S. and Europe...partly through products which previously have only existed on one of the markets," Fred J. Musone, head of Morton Automotive Safety Products (ASP), said at an analyst meeting.
"In Europe, growth will be strong, and by that I mean growth in the terms of growth companies...not companies on mature markets," he said.

New products will also boost income, he said. Currently, Autoliv and Morton are launching side window protection devices and protection against whiplash injuries. Autoliv has already won two orders for side window protection.
"Everyone can make the mathematic calculation about the szie of income that these new products can generate," Musone said. "Without knowing for sure, it could be hundreds of millions of dollars."
Autoliv will also move into new markets as it intends to be present where cars are manufactured, Musone said.
"We will exist where the production of vehicles exists and through the merger we have got the power to see this through," he said.
"Morton and Autoliv are the two companies that have been best at establishing themselves on new markets and I see no reason for us not being the largest there."
When announcing the merger, the companies mentioned new markets such as China, South Korea and Southeast Asia.
Autoliv will also restructure its operations as both it and Morton ASP have plants in Germany, the Netherlands and Britain.
"The new company won't have fewer employees in the future," Musone said. "We...will become larger. Obviously some plants must be closed down...but there won't be large closures."
Previously, Autoliv spokesman Lars Odman has said there was no overcapacity in Europe, but he has not wanted to exclude closures there.
